  "markdown": "\u003e ## Documentation Index\n\u003e \n\u003e Fetch the complete documentation index at: https://docs.langchain.com/llms.txt\n\u003e Use this file to discover all available pages before exploring further.\n\n# Agents\n\nAgents combine language models with [tools](https://docs.langchain.com/oss/python/langchain/tools) to create systems that can reason about tasks, decide which tools to use, and iteratively work towards solutions.\n\n[&#96;create_agent&#96;](https://reference.langchain.com/python/langchain/agents/factory/create_agent) provides a production-ready agent implementation.\n\n[An LLM Agent runs tools in a loop to achieve a goal](https://simonwillison.net/2025/Sep/18/agents/).\nAn agent runs until a stop condition is met - i.e., when the model emits a final output or an iteration limit is reached.\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;mermaid\n%%{\n  init: {\n    \"fontFamily\": \"monospace\",\n    \"flowchart\": {\n      \"curve\": \"curve\"\n    }\n  }\n}%%\ngraph TD\n  %% Outside the agent\n  QUERY([input])\n  LLM{model}\n  TOOL(tools)\n  ANSWER([output])\n\n  %% Main flows (no inline labels)\n  QUERY --\u003e LLM\n  LLM --\"action\"--\u003e TOOL\n  TOOL --\"observation\"--\u003e LLM\n  LLM --\"finish\"--\u003e ANSWER\n\n  classDef blueHighlight fill:#E5F4FF,stroke:#006DDD,color:#030710;\n  classDef greenHighlight fill:#F6FFDB,stroke:#6E8900,color:#2E3900;\n  class QUERY blueHighlight;\n  class ANSWER blueHighlight;\n  class LLM greenHighlight;\n  class TOOL greenHighlight;\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n[&#96;create_agent&#96;](https://reference.langchain.com/python/langchain/agents/factory/create_agent) builds a graph-based agent runtime using [LangGraph](https://docs.langchain.com/oss/python/langgraph/overview). A graph consists of nodes (steps) and edges (connections) that define how your agent processes information. The agent moves through this graph, executing nodes like the model node (which calls the model), the tools node (which executes tools), or middleware.\n\nLearn more about the [Graph API](https://docs.langchain.com/oss/python/langgraph/graph-api).\n\n## Core components\n\n### Model\n\nThe [model](https://docs.langchain.com/oss/python/langchain/models) is the reasoning engine of your agent. This is the most common and straightforward approach.\n\nTo initialize a static model from a model identifier string:\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;python\nfrom langchain.agents import create_agent\n\nagent = create_agent(\"openai:gpt-5.4\", tools=tools)\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\nModel identifier strings support automatic inference (e.g., &#96;\"gpt-5.4\"&#96; will be inferred as &#96;\"openai:gpt-5.4\"&#96;). Refer to the [reference](https://reference.langchain.com/python/langchain/chat_models/base/init_chat_model) to see a full list of model identifier string mappings.\n\nFor more control over the model configuration, initialize a model instance directly using the provider package. In this example, we use [&#96;ChatOpenAI&#96;](https://reference.langchain.com/python/langchain-openai/chat_models/base/ChatOpenAI). See [Chat models](https://docs.langchain.com/oss/python/integrations/chat) for other available chat model classes.\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;python\nfrom langchain.agents import create_agent\nfrom langchain_openai import ChatOpenAI\n\nmodel = ChatOpenAI(\n    model=\"gpt-5.4\",\n    temperature=0.1,\n    max_tokens=1000,\n    timeout=30\n    # ... (other params)\n)\nagent = create_agent(model, tools=tools)\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\nModel instances give you complete control over configuration. Use them when you need to set specific [parameters](https://docs.langchain.com/oss/python/langchain/models#parameters) like &#96;temperature&#96;, &#96;max_tokens&#96;, &#96;timeouts&#96;, &#96;base_url&#96;, and other provider-specific settings. Refer to the [reference](https://docs.langchain.com/oss/python/integrations/providers/all_providers) to see available params and methods on your model.\n\n#### Dynamic model\n\nDynamic models are selected at runtime based on the current state and context. This enables sophisticated routing logic and cost optimization.\n\nTo use a dynamic model, create middleware using the [&#96;@wrap_model_call&#96;](https://reference.langchain.com/python/langchain/agents/middleware/types/wrap_model_call) decorator that modifies the model in the request:\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;python\nfrom langchain_openai import ChatOpenAI\nfrom langchain.agents import create_agent\nfrom langchain.agents.middleware import wrap_model_call, ModelRequest, ModelResponse\n\nbasic_model = ChatOpenAI(model=\"gpt-5.4-mini\")\nadvanced_model = ChatOpenAI(model=\"gpt-5.4\")\n\n@wrap_model_call\ndef dynamic_model_selection(request: ModelRequest, handler) -\u003e ModelResponse:\n    \"\"\"Choose model based on conversation complexity.\"\"\"\n    message_count = len(request.state[\"messages\"])\n\n    if message_count \u003e 10:\n        # Use an advanced model for longer conversations\n        model = advanced_model\n    else:\n        model = basic_model\n\n    return handler(request.override(model=model))\n\nagent = create_agent(\n    model=basic_model,  # Default model\n    tools=tools,\n    middleware=[dynamic_model_selection]\n)\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\nPre-bound models (models with [&#96;bind_tools&#96;](https://reference.langchain.com/python/langchain-core/language_models/chat_models/BaseChatModel/bind_tools) already called) are not supported when using structured output. If you need dynamic model selection with structured output, ensure the models passed to the middleware are not pre-bound.\n\nFor model configuration details, see [Models](https://docs.langchain.com/oss/python/langchain/models). For dynamic model selection patterns, see [Dynamic model in middleware](https://docs.langchain.com/oss/python/langchain/middleware#dynamic-model).\n\n### Tools\n\nTools give agents the ability to take actions. Agents go beyond simple model-only tool binding by facilitating:\n\n- Multiple tool calls in sequence (triggered by a single prompt)\n- Parallel tool calls when appropriate\n- Dynamic tool selection based on previous results\n- Tool retry logic and error handling\n- State persistence across tool calls\n\nFor more information, see [Tools](https://docs.langchain.com/oss/python/langchain/tools).\n\n#### Static tools\n\nStatic tools are defined when creating the agent and remain unchanged throughout execution. This is the most common and straightforward approach.\n\nTo define an agent with static tools, pass a list of the tools to the agent.\n\nTools can be specified as plain Python functions or coroutines.\n\nThe [tool decorator](https://docs.langchain.com/oss/python/langchain/tools#create-tools) can be used to customize tool names, descriptions, argument schemas, and other properties.\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;python\nfrom langchain.tools import tool\nfrom langchain.agents import create_agent\n\n@tool\ndef search(query: str) -\u003e str:\n    \"\"\"Search for information.\"\"\"\n    return f\"Results for: {query}\"\n\n@tool\ndef get_weather(location: str) -\u003e str:\n    \"\"\"Get weather information for a location.\"\"\"\n    return f\"Weather in {location}: Sunny, 72°F\"\n\nagent = create_agent(model, tools=[search, get_weather])\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\nIf an empty tool list is provided, the agent will consist of a single LLM node without tool-calling capabilities.\n\n#### Dynamic tools\n\nWith dynamic tools, the set of tools available to the agent is modified at runtime rather than defined all upfront. Not every tool is appropriate for every situation. Too many tools may overwhelm the model (overload context) and increase errors; too few limit capabilities. Dynamic tool selection enables adapting the available toolset based on authentication state, user permissions, feature flags, or conversation stage.\n\nThere are two approaches depending on whether tools are known ahead of time:\n\n## Filtering pre-registered tools\n\nWhen all possible tools are known at agent creation time, you can pre-register them and dynamically filter which ones are exposed to the model based on state, permissions, or context.\n\n## State\n\nEnable advanced tools only after certain conversation milestones:\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;python\nfrom langchain.agents import create_agent\nfrom langchain.agents.middleware import wrap_model_call, ModelRequest, ModelResponse\nfrom typing import Callable\n\n@wrap_model_call\ndef state_based_tools(\n    request: ModelRequest,\n    handler: Callable[[ModelRequest], ModelResponse]\n) -\u003e ModelResponse:\n    \"\"\"Filter tools based on conversation State.\"\"\"\n    # Read from State: check if user has authenticated\n    state = request.state\n    is_authenticated = state.get(\"authenticated\", False)\n    message_count = len(state[\"messages\"])\n\n    # Only enable sensitive tools after authentication\n    if not is_authenticated:\n        tools = [t for t in request.tools if t.name.startswith(\"public_\")]\n        request = request.override(tools=tools)\n    elif message_count \u003c 5:\n        # Limit tools early in conversation\n        tools = [t for t in request.tools if t.name != \"advanced_search\"]\n        request = request.override(tools=tools)\n\n    return handler(request)\n\nagent = create_agent(\n    model=\"gpt-5.4\",\n    tools=[public_search, private_search, advanced_search],\n    middleware=[state_based_tools]\n)\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n## Store\n\nFilter tools based on user preferences or feature flags in Store:\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;python\nfrom dataclasses import dataclass\nfrom langchain.agents import create_agent\nfrom langchain.agents.middleware import wrap_model_call, ModelRequest, ModelResponse\nfrom typing import Callable\nfrom langgraph.store.memory import InMemoryStore\n\n@dataclass\nclass Context:\n    user_id: str\n\n@wrap_model_call\ndef store_based_tools(\n    request: ModelRequest,\n    handler: Callable[[ModelRequest], ModelResponse]\n) -\u003e ModelResponse:\n    \"\"\"Filter tools based on Store preferences.\"\"\"\n    user_id = request.runtime.context.user_id\n\n    # Read from Store: get user's enabled features\n    store = request.runtime.store\n    feature_flags = store.get((\"features\",), user_id)\n\n    if feature_flags:\n        enabled_features = feature_flags.value.get(\"enabled_tools\", [])\n        # Only include tools that are enabled for this user\n        tools = [t for t in request.tools if t.name in enabled_features]\n        request = request.override(tools=tools)\n\n    return handler(request)\n\nagent = create_agent(\n    model=\"gpt-5.4\",\n    tools=[search_tool, analysis_tool, export_tool],\n    middleware=[store_based_tools],\n    context_schema=Context,\n    store=InMemoryStore()\n)\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n## Runtime Context\n\nFilter tools based on user permissions from Runtime Context:\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;python\nfrom dataclasses import dataclass\nfrom langchain.agents import create_agent\nfrom langchain.agents.middleware import wrap_model_call, ModelRequest, ModelResponse\nfrom typing import Callable\n\n@dataclass\nclass Context:\n    user_role: str\n\n@wrap_model_call\ndef context_based_tools(\n    request: ModelRequest,\n    handler: Callable[[ModelRequest], ModelResponse]\n) -\u003e ModelResponse:\n    \"\"\"Filter tools based on Runtime Context permissions.\"\"\"\n    # Read from Runtime Context: get user role\n    if request.runtime is None or request.runtime.context is None:\n        # If no context provided, default to viewer (most restrictive)\n        user_role = \"viewer\"\n    else:\n        user_role = request.runtime.context.user_role\n\n    if user_role == \"admin\":\n        # Admins get all tools\n        pass\n    elif user_role == \"editor\":\n        # Editors can't delete\n        tools = [t for t in request.tools if t.name != \"delete_data\"]\n        request = request.override(tools=tools)\n    else:\n        # Viewers get read-only tools\n        tools = [t for t in request.tools if t.name.startswith(\"read_\")]\n        request = request.override(tools=tools)\n\n    return handler(request)\n\nagent = create_agent(\n    model=\"gpt-5.4\",\n    tools=[read_data, write_data, delete_data],\n    middleware=[context_based_tools],\n    context_schema=Context\n)\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\nThis approach is best when:\n\n- All possible tools are known at compile/startup time\n- You want to filter based on permissions, feature flags, or conversation state\n- Tools are static but their availability is dynamic\n\nSee [Dynamically selecting tools](https://docs.langchain.com/oss/python/langchain/middleware/custom#dynamically-selecting-tools) for more examples.\n\n## Runtime tool registration\n\nWhen tools are discovered or created at runtime (e.g., loaded from an MCP server, generated based on user data, or fetched from a remote registry), you need to both register the tools and handle their execution dynamically.\n\nThis requires two middleware hooks:\n\n1. &#96;wrap_model_call&#96; - Add the dynamic tools to the request\n2. &#96;wrap_tool_call&#96; - Handle execution of the dynamically added tools\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;python\nfrom langchain.tools import tool\nfrom langchain.agents import create_agent\nfrom langchain.agents.middleware import AgentMiddleware, ModelRequest, ToolCallRequest\n\n# A tool that will be added dynamically at runtime\n@tool\ndef calculate_tip(bill_amount: float, tip_percentage: float = 20.0) -\u003e str:\n    \"\"\"Calculate the tip amount for a bill.\"\"\"\n    tip = bill_amount * (tip_percentage / 100)\n    return f\"Tip: ${tip:.2f}, Total: ${bill_amount + tip:.2f}\"\n\nclass DynamicToolMiddleware(AgentMiddleware):\n    \"\"\"Middleware that registers and handles dynamic tools.\"\"\"\n\n    def wrap_model_call(self, request: ModelRequest, handler):\n        # Add dynamic tool to the request\n        # This could be loaded from an MCP server, database, etc.\n        updated = request.override(tools=[*request.tools, calculate_tip])\n        return handler(updated)\n\n    def wrap_tool_call(self, request: ToolCallRequest, handler):\n        # Handle execution of the dynamic tool\n        if request.tool_call[\"name\"] == \"calculate_tip\":\n            return handler(request.override(tool=calculate_tip))\n        return handler(request)\n\nagent = create_agent(\n    model=\"gpt-4o\",\n    tools=[get_weather],  # Only static tools registered here\n    middleware=[DynamicToolMiddleware()],\n)\n\n# The agent can now use both get_weather AND calculate_tip\nresult = agent.invoke({\n    \"messages\": [{\"role\": \"user\", \"content\": \"Calculate a 20% tip on $85\"}]\n})\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\nThis approach is best when:\n\n- Tools are discovered at runtime (e.g., from an MCP server)\n- Tools are generated dynamically based on user data or configuration\n- You're integrating with external tool registries\n\nThe &#96;wrap_tool_call&#96; hook is required for runtime-registered tools because the agent needs to know how to execute tools that weren't in the original tool list. Without it, the agent won't know how to invoke the dynamically added tool.\n\nTo learn more about tools, see [Tools](https://docs.langchain.com/oss/python/langchain/tools).\n\n#### Tool error handling\n\nTo customize how tool errors are handled, use the [&#96;@wrap_tool_call&#96;](https://reference.langchain.com/python/langchain/agents/middleware/types/wrap_tool_call) decorator to create middleware:\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;python\nfrom langchain.agents import create_agent\nfrom langchain.agents.middleware import wrap_tool_call\nfrom langchain.messages import ToolMessage\n\n@wrap_tool_call\ndef handle_tool_errors(request, handler):\n    \"\"\"Handle tool execution errors with custom messages.\"\"\"\n    try:\n        return handler(request)\n    except Exception as e:\n        # Return a custom error message to the model\n        return ToolMessage(\n            content=f\"Tool error: Please check your input and try again. ({str(e)})\",\n            tool_call_id=request.tool_call[\"id\"]\n        )\n\nagent = create_agent(\n    model=\"gpt-5.4\",\n    tools=[search, get_weather],\n    middleware=[handle_tool_errors]\n)\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\nThe agent will return a [&#96;ToolMessage&#96;](https://reference.langchain.com/python/langchain-core/messages/tool/ToolMessage) with the custom error message when a tool fails:\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;python\n[\n    ...\n    ToolMessage(\n        content=\"Tool error: Please check your input and try again. (division by zero)\",\n        tool_call_id=\"...\"\n    ),\n    ...\n]\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n#### Tool use in the ReAct loop\n\nAgents follow the ReAct (\"Reasoning + Acting\") pattern, alternating between brief reasoning steps with targeted tool calls and feeding the resulting observations into subsequent decisions until they can deliver a final answer.\n\n## Example of ReAct loop\n\nPrompt: Identify the current most popular wireless headphones and verify availability.\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n================================ Human Message =================================\n\nFind the most popular wireless headphones right now and check if they're in stock\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n- Reasoning: \"Popularity is time-sensitive, I need to use the provided search tool.\"\n- Acting: Call &#96;search_products(\"wireless headphones\")&#96;\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n================================== Ai Message ==================================\nTool Calls:\n  search_products (call_abc123)\n Call ID: call_abc123\n  Args:\n    query: wireless headphones\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n================================= Tool Message =================================\n\nFound 5 products matching \"wireless headphones\". Top 5 results: WH-1000XM5, ...\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n- Reasoning: \"I need to confirm availability for the top-ranked item before answering.\"\n- Acting: Call &#96;check_inventory(\"WH-1000XM5\")&#96;\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n================================== Ai Message ==================================\nTool Calls:\n  check_inventory (call_def456)\n Call ID: call_def456\n  Args:\n    product_id: WH-1000XM5\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n================================= Tool Message =================================\n\nProduct WH-1000XM5: 10 units in stock\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n- Reasoning: \"I have the most popular model and its stock status. I can now answer the user's question.\"\n- Acting: Produce final answer\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n================================== Ai Message ==================================\n\nI found wireless headphones (model WH-1000XM5) with 10 units in stock...\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n### System prompt\n\nYou can shape how your agent approaches tasks by providing a prompt. The [&#96;system_prompt&#96;](https://reference.langchain.com/python/langchain/agents/#langchain.agents.create_agent(system_prompt)) parameter can be provided as a string:\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;python\nagent = create_agent(\n    model,\n    tools,\n    system_prompt=\"You are a helpful assistant. Be concise and accurate.\"\n)\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\nWhen no [&#96;system_prompt&#96;](https://reference.langchain.com/python/langchain/agents/#langchain.agents.create_agent(system_prompt)) is provided, the agent will infer its task from the messages directly.\n\nThe [&#96;system_prompt&#96;](https://reference.langchain.com/python/langchain/agents/#langchain.agents.create_agent(system_prompt)) parameter accepts either a &#96;str&#96; or a [&#96;SystemMessage&#96;](https://reference.langchain.com/python/langchain-core/messages/system/SystemMessage). Using a &#96;SystemMessage&#96; gives you more control over the prompt structure, which is useful for provider-specific features like [Anthropic's prompt caching](https://docs.langchain.com/oss/python/integrations/chat/anthropic#prompt-caching):\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;python\nfrom langchain.agents import create_agent\nfrom langchain.messages import SystemMessage, HumanMessage\n\nliterary_agent = create_agent(\n    model=\"google_genai:gemini-3.1-pro-preview\",\n    system_prompt=SystemMessage(\n        content=[\n            {\n                \"type\": \"text\",\n                \"text\": \"You are an AI assistant tasked with analyzing literary works.\",\n            },\n            {\n                \"type\": \"text\",\n                \"text\": \"\u003cthe entire contents of 'Pride and Prejudice'\u003e\",\n                \"cache_control\": {\"type\": \"ephemeral\"}\n            }\n        ]\n    )\n)\n\nresult = literary_agent.invoke(\n    {\"messages\": [HumanMessage(\"Analyze the major themes in 'Pride and Prejudice'.\")]}\n)\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\nThe &#96;cache_control&#96; field with &#96;{\"type\": \"ephemeral\"}&#96; tells Anthropic to cache that content block, reducing latency and costs for repeated requests that use the same system prompt.\n\n#### Dynamic system prompt\n\nFor more advanced use cases where you need to modify the system prompt based on runtime context or agent state, you can use [middleware](https://docs.langchain.com/oss/python/langchain/middleware).\n\nThe [&#96;@dynamic_prompt&#96;](https://reference.langchain.com/python/langchain/agents/middleware/types/dynamic_prompt) decorator creates middleware that generates system prompts based on the model request:\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;python\nfrom typing import TypedDict\n\nfrom langchain.agents import create_agent\nfrom langchain.agents.middleware import dynamic_prompt, ModelRequest\n\nclass Context(TypedDict):\n    user_role: str\n\n@dynamic_prompt\ndef user_role_prompt(request: ModelRequest) -\u003e str:\n    \"\"\"Generate system prompt based on user role.\"\"\"\n    user_role = request.runtime.context.get(\"user_role\", \"user\")\n    base_prompt = \"You are a helpful assistant.\"\n\n    if user_role == \"expert\":\n        return f\"{base_prompt} Provide detailed technical responses.\"\n    elif user_role == \"beginner\":\n        return f\"{base_prompt} Explain concepts simply and avoid jargon.\"\n\n    return base_prompt\n\nagent = create_agent(\n    model=\"gpt-5.4\",\n    tools=[web_search],\n    middleware=[user_role_prompt],\n    context_schema=Context\n)\n\n# The system prompt will be set dynamically based on context\nresult = agent.invoke(\n    {\"messages\": [{\"role\": \"user\", \"content\": \"Explain machine learning\"}]},\n    context={\"user_role\": \"expert\"}\n)\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\nFor more details on message types and formatting, see [Messages](https://docs.langchain.com/oss/python/langchain/messages). For comprehensive middleware documentation, see [Middleware](https://docs.langchain.com/oss/python/langchain/middleware).\n\n### Name\n\nSet an optional [&#96;name&#96;](https://reference.langchain.com/python/langchain/agents/factory/create_agent) for the agent. This is used as the node identifier when adding the agent as a subgraph in [multi-agent systems](https://docs.langchain.com/oss/python/langchain/multi-agent):\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;python\nagent = create_agent(\n    model,\n    tools,\n    name=\"research_assistant\"\n)\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\nPrefer &#96;snake_case&#96; for agent names (e.g., &#96;research_assistant&#96; instead of &#96;Research Assistant&#96;). Some model providers reject names containing spaces or special characters with errors. Using alphanumeric characters, underscores, and hyphens only ensures compatibility across all providers. The same applies to [tool names](https://docs.langchain.com/oss/python/langchain/tools).\n\n## Invocation\n\nYou can invoke an agent by passing an update to its [&#96;State&#96;](https://docs.langchain.com/oss/python/langgraph/graph-api#state). All agents include a [sequence of messages](https://docs.langchain.com/oss/python/langgraph/use-graph-api#messagesstate) in their state; to invoke the agent, pass a new message:\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;python\nresult = agent.invoke(\n    {\"messages\": [{\"role\": \"user\", \"content\": \"What's the weather in San Francisco?\"}]}\n)\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\nFor streaming steps and / or tokens from the agent, refer to the [streaming](https://docs.langchain.com/oss/python/langchain/streaming) guide.\n\nOtherwise, the agent follows the LangGraph [Graph API](https://docs.langchain.com/oss/python/langgraph/use-graph-api) and supports all associated methods, such as &#96;stream&#96; and &#96;invoke&#96;.\n\nUse [LangSmith](https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/home) to trace, debug, and evaluate your agents.\n\n## Advanced concepts\n\n### Structured output\n\nIn some situations, you may want the agent to return an output in a specific format. LangChain provides strategies for structured output via the [&#96;response_format&#96;](https://reference.langchain.com/python/langchain/agents/factory/create_agent) parameter.\n\n#### ToolStrategy\n\n&#96;ToolStrategy&#96; uses artificial tool calling to generate structured output. This works with any model that supports tool calling. &#96;ToolStrategy&#96; should be used when provider-native structured output (via [&#96;ProviderStrategy&#96;](https://docs.langchain.com/oss/python/langchain/agents#providerstrategy)) is not available or reliable.\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;python\nfrom pydantic import BaseModel\nfrom langchain.agents import create_agent\nfrom langchain.agents.structured_output import ToolStrategy\n\nclass ContactInfo(BaseModel):\n    name: str\n    email: str\n    phone: str\n\nagent = create_agent(\n    model=\"gpt-5.4-mini\",\n    tools=[search_tool],\n    response_format=ToolStrategy(ContactInfo)\n)\n\nresult = agent.invoke({\n    \"messages\": [{\"role\": \"user\", \"content\": \"Extract contact info from: John Doe, john@example.com, (555) 123-4567\"}]\n})\n\nresult[\"structured_response\"]\n# ContactInfo(name='John Doe', email='john@example.com', phone='(555) 123-4567')\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n#### ProviderStrategy\n\n&#96;ProviderStrategy&#96; uses the model provider's native structured output generation. This is more reliable but only works with providers that support native structured output:\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;python\nfrom langchain.agents.structured_output import ProviderStrategy\n\nagent = create_agent(\n    model=\"gpt-5.4\",\n    response_format=ProviderStrategy(ContactInfo)\n)\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\nAs of &#96;langchain 1.0&#96;, simply passing a schema (e.g., &#96;response_format=ContactInfo&#96;) will default to &#96;ProviderStrategy&#96; if the model supports native structured output. It will fall back to &#96;ToolStrategy&#96; otherwise.\n\nTo learn about structured output, see [Structured output](https://docs.langchain.com/oss/python/langchain/structured-output).\n\n### Memory\n\nAgents maintain conversation history automatically through the message state. You can also configure the agent to use a custom state schema to remember additional information during the conversation.\n\nInformation stored in the state can be thought of as the [short-term memory](https://docs.langchain.com/oss/python/langchain/short-term-memory) of the agent:\n\nCustom state schemas must extend [&#96;AgentState&#96;](https://reference.langchain.com/python/langchain/agents/middleware/types/AgentState) as a &#96;TypedDict&#96;.\n\nThere are two ways to define custom state:\n\n1. Via [middleware](https://docs.langchain.com/oss/python/langchain/middleware) (preferred)\n2. Via [&#96;state_schema&#96;](https://reference.langchain.com/python/langchain/middleware/#langchain.agents.middleware.AgentMiddleware.state_schema) on [&#96;create_agent&#96;](https://reference.langchain.com/python/langchain/agents/factory/create_agent)\n\n#### Defining state via middleware\n\nUse middleware to define custom state when your custom state needs to be accessed by specific middleware hooks and tools attached to said middleware.\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;python\nfrom langchain.agents import AgentState\nfrom langchain.agents.middleware import AgentMiddleware\nfrom typing import Any\n\nclass CustomState(AgentState):\n    user_preferences: dict\n\nclass CustomMiddleware(AgentMiddleware):\n    state_schema = CustomState\n    tools = [tool1, tool2]\n\n    def before_model(self, state: CustomState, runtime) -\u003e dict[str, Any] | None:\n        ...\n\nagent = create_agent(\n    model,\n    tools=tools,\n    middleware=[CustomMiddleware()]\n)\n\n# The agent can now track additional state beyond messages\nresult = agent.invoke({\n    \"messages\": [{\"role\": \"user\", \"content\": \"I prefer technical explanations\"}],\n    \"user_preferences\": {\"style\": \"technical\", \"verbosity\": \"detailed\"},\n})\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n#### Defining state via &#96;state_schema&#96;\n\nUse the [&#96;state_schema&#96;](https://reference.langchain.com/python/langchain/middleware/#langchain.agents.middleware.AgentMiddleware.state_schema) parameter as a shortcut to define custom state that is only used in tools.\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;python\nfrom langchain.agents import AgentState\n\nclass CustomState(AgentState):\n    user_preferences: dict\n\nagent = create_agent(\n    model,\n    tools=[tool1, tool2],\n    state_schema=CustomState\n)\n# The agent can now track additional state beyond messages\nresult = agent.invoke({\n    \"messages\": [{\"role\": \"user\", \"content\": \"I prefer technical explanations\"}],\n    \"user_preferences\": {\"style\": \"technical\", \"verbosity\": \"detailed\"},\n})\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\nAs of &#96;langchain 1.0&#96;, custom state schemas must be &#96;TypedDict&#96; types. Pydantic models and dataclasses are no longer supported. See the [v1 migration guide](https://docs.langchain.com/oss/python/migrate/langchain-v1#state-type-restrictions) for more details.\n\nDefining custom state via middleware is preferred over defining it via [&#96;state_schema&#96;](https://reference.langchain.com/python/langchain/middleware/#langchain.agents.middleware.AgentMiddleware.state_schema) on [&#96;create_agent&#96;](https://reference.langchain.com/python/langchain/agents/factory/create_agent) because it allows you to keep state extensions conceptually scoped to the relevant middleware and tools.\n\n[&#96;state_schema&#96;](https://reference.langchain.com/python/langchain/middleware/#langchain.agents.middleware.AgentMiddleware.state_schema) is still supported for backwards compatibility on [&#96;create_agent&#96;](https://reference.langchain.com/python/langchain/agents/factory/create_agent).\n\nTo learn more about memory, see [Memory](https://docs.langchain.com/oss/python/concepts/memory). For information on implementing long-term memory that persists across sessions, see [Long-term memory](https://docs.langchain.com/oss/python/langchain/long-term-memory).\n\n### Streaming\n\nWe've seen how the agent can be called with &#96;invoke&#96; to get a final response. If the agent executes multiple steps, this may take a while. To show intermediate progress, we can stream back messages as they occur.\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;python\nfrom langchain.messages import AIMessage, HumanMessage\n\nfor chunk in agent.stream({\n    \"messages\": [{\"role\": \"user\", \"content\": \"Search for AI news and summarize the findings\"}]\n}, stream_mode=\"values\"):\n    # Each chunk contains the full state at that point\n    latest_message = chunk[\"messages\"][-1]\n    if latest_message.content:\n        if isinstance(latest_message, HumanMessage):\n            print(f\"User: {latest_message.content}\")\n        elif isinstance(latest_message, AIMessage):\n            print(f\"Agent: {latest_message.content}\")\n    elif latest_message.tool_calls:\n        print(f\"Calling tools: {[tc['name'] for tc in latest_message.tool_calls]}\")\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\nFor more details on streaming, see [Streaming](https://docs.langchain.com/oss/python/langchain/streaming).\n\n### Middleware\n\n[Middleware](https://docs.langchain.com/oss/python/langchain/middleware) provides powerful extensibility for customizing agent behavior at different stages of execution. You can use middleware to:\n\n- Process state before the model is called (e.g., message trimming, context injection)\n- Modify or validate the model's response (e.g., guardrails, content filtering)\n- Handle tool execution errors with custom logic\n- Implement dynamic model selection based on state or context\n- Add custom logging, monitoring, or analytics\n\nMiddleware integrates seamlessly into the agent's execution, allowing you to intercept and modify data flow at key points without changing the core agent logic.\n\nFor comprehensive middleware documentation including decorators like [&#96;@before_model&#96;](https://reference.langchain.com/python/langchain/agents/middleware/types/before_model), [&#96;@after_model&#96;](https://reference.langchain.com/python/langchain/agents/middleware/types/after_model), and [&#96;@wrap_tool_call&#96;](https://reference.langchain.com/python/langchain/agents/middleware/types/wrap_tool_call), see [Middleware](https://docs.langchain.com/oss/python/langchain/middleware).\n\n---\n\n[Connect these docs](https://docs.langchain.com/use-these-docs) to Claude, VSCode, and more via MCP for real-time answers.\n\n[Edit this page on GitHub](https://github.com/langchain-ai/docs/edit/main/src/oss/langchain/agents.mdx) or [file an issue](https://github.com/langchain-ai/docs/issues/new/choose).",

_**Agent (claude-sonnet-4-6)**_

Here's my understanding of the project:

**What we're building:** A conversational travel planning agent powered by LangChain's `create_agent` API that users interact with in the terminal (phase 1), with a Vercel-hosted UI coming later (phase 2).

**The 4 tools:**

1. **Flight Finder** -- Helps users search for flights (origin, destination, dates, etc.)
2. **Hotel Finder** -- Helps users search for hotel accommodations at their destination
3. **Itinerary Planner** -- Generates a day-by-day activity plan for the trip
4. **Budget Estimator** -- Pulls together costs (flights, hotels, activities, food, etc.) into an overall trip budget estimate

**Agent behavior:** The user describes their trip in natural language, and the agent uses the ReAct loop to reason about which tools to call -- potentially chaining them together (e.g., find flights and hotels first, then use those results to build an itinerary and budget).

**A few questions before we start:**

1. **LLM provider** -- Do you have a preference? OpenAI (GPT), Anthropic (Claude), Google (Gemini)? This affects which API key you'll need.

2. **Tool data sources** -- For the flight and hotel tools, should these return mock/simulated data for now, or do you want to integrate with real APIs (like Amadeus, Google Flights, etc.) from the start?

3. **Conversation memory** -- Should the agent remember context within a terminal session (e.g., "I said I wanted to go to Tokyo" referenced later), or is each prompt standalone?

4. **Vercel plans** -- Since LangChain is Python and Vercel typically serves JS/TS frontends, are you thinking a separate Python backend (e.g., FastAPI) with a Next.js frontend, or something else?

_**Agent (claude-sonnet-4-6)**_

Great questions back -- here are my recommendations:

**1. LLM Provider: OpenAI (GPT)**

I'd recommend OpenAI for this project. It has the strongest tool-calling support in LangChain, the largest ecosystem of examples, and the `create_agent` docs lean heavily on it. GPT-4o-mini is a good balance of cost and quality for a tool-heavy agent like this.

**2. Real API: Amadeus**

Amadeus is the go-to for travel apps. They have a **free self-service tier** that gives you access to:
- **Flight Offers Search** -- real flight data (prices, airlines, routes)
- **Hotel List & Offers** -- hotel search by city with pricing

You just sign up at [developers.amadeus.com](https://developers.amadeus.com) and get API keys immediately. The test environment uses real-ish data without needing a paid plan. There's also a solid Python SDK (`amadeus`). For the itinerary and budget tools, those won't need an external API -- the LLM itself can reason over the flight/hotel data to build itineraries and estimate budgets.

**3. Conversation Memory: Yes**

We'll configure the agent with message history so it tracks the full conversation within a session. The user can say "find flights to Tokyo" and then later "now find hotels there" and the agent will know "there" means Tokyo.

**4. Architecture**

- **Now (phase 1):** Python terminal app with LangChain agent
- **Later (phase 2):** FastAPI backend serving the agent + Next.js frontend on Vercel

---

**So the stack will be:**

| Layer | Tech |
|---|---|
| LLM | OpenAI (GPT-4o-mini) |
| Agent framework | LangChain (`create_agent`) |
| Flight & hotel data | Amadeus API |
| Itinerary & budget | LLM reasoning over collected data |
| Terminal interface | Python (phase 1) |
| Backend API | FastAPI (phase 2) |
| Frontend | Next.js on Vercel (phase 2) |

Does this all sound good? If so, I'll also need to know -- do you already have an OpenAI API key and/or an Amadeus API key, or do you need to go grab those before we start coding?

_**Agent (claude-sonnet-4-6)**_

Before I draft the system prompt, I want to make sure I get the personality and behavior right. A few questions:

1. **Tone & personality** -- Should the agent be casual and friendly (like a travel-savvy friend), professional and concise (like a travel consultant), or somewhere in between?

2. **Scope boundaries** -- When a user asks something completely unrelated to travel (e.g., "help me write a resume"), should the agent politely decline and redirect, or be flexible?

3. **Proactive suggestions** -- Should the agent proactively suggest things the user hasn't asked for? For example, if someone says "I want to go to Tokyo in December," should it volunteer tips like "December is cold, pack warm clothes" or "that's peak season, book early"?

4. **Multi-destination trips** -- Should it handle trips with multiple stops (e.g., "I want to fly to Paris, then train to Amsterdam, then fly home"), or focus on single-destination trips for now?

5. **Traveler details** -- Should the agent ask about group size, travel class preferences (economy/business), budget range, or dietary/accessibility needs upfront, or only when relevant?

6. **Currency** -- Should it default to USD for budget estimates, or ask the user their preferred currency?

7. **Itinerary style** -- Should itineraries be packed/activity-heavy, relaxed, or should the agent ask what the user prefers?

---

**SYSTEM PROMPT:**

> You are a professional travel planning assistant. You are friendly, approachable, and easy to communicate with — like a knowledgeable travel consultant who genuinely enjoys helping people plan great trips.
> 
> **Scope:**
> You only help with travel-related topics. If a user asks about something unrelated to travel planning, politely let them know you're focused on travel and redirect the conversation.
> 
> **Your capabilities:**
> You help users plan trips by finding flights, finding hotels, building itineraries, and estimating budgets. You can handle multi-destination trips — if a user wants to visit multiple cities or countries in one trip, coordinate across all legs seamlessly.
> 
> **How you interact:**
> - Make smart assumptions for common parameters (e.g., economy class, 1 traveler, standard hotel) so users don't face a wall of questions. Always let them know what you assumed and offer to adjust if they want something different.
> - Be proactive — share helpful tips, travel insights, and suggestions (e.g., "December is peak season in Tokyo, so booking early is a good idea"). But always prioritize what the user is asking for over unsolicited advice.
> - When a user asks for an itinerary, don't jump straight into a full day-by-day plan. First share some highlights and notable things about the destination, then ask what kinds of experiences they're looking for (culture, food, adventure, relaxation, nightlife, etc.). If they're not sure, walk them through a few questions to help them figure out what they'd enjoy.
> 
> **Currency:**
> Default to USD for all budget estimates and pricing. When presenting costs, also mention the equivalent in the local currency of the destination. If the user requests a different currency, switch to that.
> 
> **Tool usage:**
> You have access to tools for searching flights, searching hotels, planning itineraries, and estimating budgets. Use them when the user's request calls for real data. Don't fabricate flight numbers, prices, or hotel names — use your tools to get actual information.
> 
> **Conversation style:**
> - Keep responses well-organized and scannable (use bullet points, short paragraphs)
> - Be concise but thorough — don't overwhelm, but don't leave out important details
> - Remember context from earlier in the conversation so users don't have to repeat themselves

---

from main import agent

def run_conversation(turns):
    history = []
    for user_input in turns:
        print(f'You: {user_input}')
        history.append({'role': 'user', 'content': user_input})
        for chunk in agent.stream({'messages': history}, stream_mode='updates'):
            for node, updates in chunk.items():
                if node == 'tools':
                    for msg in updates['messages']:
                        print(f'  >>> Calling: {msg.name}')
                elif node == 'model':
                    msg = updates['messages'][-1]
                    if msg.content:
                        print(f'Agent: {msg.content}')
                        history.append({'role': 'assistant', 'content': msg.content})
        print()

print('=' * 60)
print('TEST 1: FLIGHT SEARCH')
print('=' * 60)
run_conversation([
    'Find me round-trip flights from New York to Tokyo departing July 10, returning July 24'
])

print('=' * 60)
print('TEST 2: HOTEL SEARCH')
print('=' * 60)
run_conversation([
    'Find me hotels in Tokyo for July 10 to July 24, 2 guests'
])

print('=' * 60)
print('TEST 3: ITINERARY PLANNER')
print('=' * 60)
run_conversation([
    'I want a 7-day itinerary for Tokyo, I love food and culture'
])

print('=' * 60)
print('TEST 4: BUDGET ESTIMATOR')
print('=' * 60)
run_conversation([
    'Estimate the budget for a 14-day trip to Tokyo for 2 people, moderate travel style'
])
"
